title: Part 1: Theme Switcher with Persistent Preference
summary: How I built a light/dark mode toggle that remembers your choice using localStorage.
content: I needed to support both light and dark themes for my portfolio website, and I wanted to give users the ability to switch between them.
First, before even getting to the theme switcher, I set up the CSS for both themes,
one as root for light mode, and a seperate for dark mode. Since custom properties are inherited
the rest of the CSS doesn't need to be duplicated, and I can just change the root variables to switch themes.
On the JS side I created a function to toggle the theme, and I added an event listener to the theme switcher button.
I also wanted to make sure that the user's preference was remembered, so I used localStorage to store the current theme. When the page loads
I check localStorage for a saved theme and apply it if it exists.
If localStorage doesn't have a saved theme, I deafult to the dark-theme (i think it looks better sry).
The hardest part was making sure that the light/dark mode button actually persisted between sites
to test i made sure to switch to light mode, and change pages, makiung sure light mode persisted and the button was still correct

title: Part 3: Dynamic Blog Section
summary: Loading and rendering blog posts from a JSON file instead of hardcoding them into HTML.
content: Before part 3, I only had a placeholder blog to make sure my css looked clean
the goal for this part was to replace the hardcoded blog with dynamic content loaded from a JSON file.
just rendering one post was fairly simple, but the difficulty came when adding multiple posts and sort them by date.
The first step to sorting was converting the date string into an actual objecet, so I could compare them and sort them in descending order.
The latest post badge was supprisingly easy, as I already had a sorted array of posts
All i needed to do was look at the first post in the array and add a badge to it, and remove the badge from all other posts.
The last piece was making the read more function
Initially I wanted to centre the full content, and dim the rest of the page
This ended up being a bit complicated, and I decided to finish it at the end, however the rest of the assigment took some time and I have other course work as well
so i settled on just expaning the card to show the full content, and adding a read less button to collapse it back down.(although I might try to finish this later after exams are over)

title: Part 4: Contact Form Validation
summary: Validating name, email, and message fields on the client side with inline error messages.
content: The contact form needed to validate three fields before it could submit: A non-empty name, a email formated correctly, and a message of at least 20 charecters
If these werent valid, an error message should appear which will disapear when a correct input is given. If all are successfull
a sucess message takes the place of the form(right now I have a simulated version of a submission but i would like to be able ro actually receive submissions)
First I had to intercept the message using preventDefault inside a submit event listener. Next I used a showError and clearError function. One to display the error
and another to clear errors when a user types. When the submit button is pressed the submit handler, a check is made for all three fields making sure all three pass
and only displaying the sucess message after all three are cleared.

title: Part 5: Projects / Blog Filter
summary: Adding live search filtering to both the Projects and Blog pages without any page reloads.
content: Using the search bar already added, functionality is needed to actually sort through blog and project posts
as the user types, the page should automaticaly show the matching cards and hide the rest without a page reload
and I needed to match against btoh title and category. If no results are found, a no results message will show.
The logic runs a check for every key stroke inside the search box, where it will check if a cards title or category is typed
and will show those specific cards. A count was made to check for how many cards are still visible
and if this count reaches 0, the no results message will show. The hardest part of this section was trying to get the logic to work on two seperate pages
each with seperate structures. My projects page has static cards with attributes present from the start
but my blog page dynamically loads cards using JavaScript. To solve this I made the filter callable from two different places
immediately for projects, and from right inside the blog-rendering code itself, right after all the cards are created.
